podcast.body: The lead-off track from Tin Machine's self-titled debut, which reached number four on Billboard's modern rock tracks chart in the summer of 1989. It showcased the band's noisy rock sound, reflecting their art punk influences. "Under the god, the lead-off track from Tin Machine reached number four on modern rock tracks in the summer of 89."

podcast.body: This single from Tin Machine's self-titled debut album exemplifies their heavy and angular sound, representing Bowie's pivot towards more primal rock music, years before grunge and alternative rock would dominate the airwaves. "If you don't know the band, here's a sample. This is a single from their self-titled debut album. It's called Under the God."
